title: P2 future: deploy automation wires typed scope through systemd unit once Spec 104 Phase 1 lands
notes:
Once Spec 104 lands (other agent owns), the daemon will read typed-scope env vars (or a scope config file) at boot. Deploy automation must be updated to (a) write the canonical ProjectIdentity scope to the systemd unit as Environment= lines or via EnvironmentFile=, (b) extend patch_service_unit_execstart to NOT clobber those lines, (c) extend the install-time first-boot recipe in production-deployment-guide.md, (d) verify via deploy-smoke-check.sh that scope reaches /v1/health (e.g., /v1/project/identity).

Why P2 not P1: deploy automation currently has no scope interaction (scripts/install-daemon.sh, install-self-hosted-runner.sh, safe-disk-cleanup.sh, deploy-smoke-check.sh all orthogonal to Spec 104). This is a forward-compatibility landing pad, not a current bug.

Spec 111 does NOT cover this — Spec 111 is agent-cold-start bootstrap via ProjectIdentity at session start, not daemon-boot scope resolution from systemd. The two are different layers.

Blocked-by: Spec 104 Phase 1 (universal typed scope reference) landing in focusa-core + focusa-api.

Acceptance criteria:
1. systemd unit file ships with scope env vars / EnvironmentFile= that the install script writes idempotently.
2. patch_service_unit_execstart preserves any Environment= lines that the script owns.
3. /v1/health (or /v1/project/identity) probe in deploy-smoke-check.sh confirms scope is non-empty and matches the project_root.
4. tests/release_deploy_automation_static_test.sh updated to assert scope handling.

Evidence citations required on close: link to Spec 104 PR / commit hash that introduced the scope contract.

title: BUG: focusa_predict_recent + trajectory_handle bleed across projects (no project_root scoping)
description:
Cross-project state bleed observed in a philoveracity-launch-pages Pi session:

1. focusa_predict_recent returned predictions scoped to project=/home/planmarr/plan-the-marriage continuity=focusa-cont-plan-the-marriage-... while the active session project_root was /home/focusadev/philoveracity-launch-pages. The tool has NO project_root parameter and returns globally most-recent predictions, ignoring the active project.

2. focusa_trajectory_view (and TRAJECTORY_CONTEXT prefix injected into handle ECS blocks) returned HLT=Run PlanTheMarriage as a profitable course business... on calls intended for the philoveracity-launch-pages scope. Daemon appears to key trajectory/prediction reads by continuity_id / session fingerprint, NOT by project_root.

Repro: In a Pi session bound to project_root=/home/focusadev/philoveracity-launch-pages, call focusa_predict_recent (no project_root param) — returns another projects predictions. Call focusa_trajectory_view — may return another projects HLT via trajectory handle context.

Expected: focusa_predict_recent, focusa_trajectory_view, and handle ECS TRAJECTORY_CONTEXT rehydration MUST filter by the same project_root used to bootstrap the session. No cross-project HLT/prediction/metacog bleed.

Fix direction: Add project_root parameter to focusa_predict_recent (and any read that lacks one); enforce active project_root as the filter key for trajectory handle rehydration; do not fall back to most-recent-across-projects when continuity_id is unbound.

Related: focusa-l38o (trajectory wrapper cache bleed), focusa-oh7t (focusa_decide rejected as attentive).

description: Real Mac v0.9.33 test exposed portability gaps. First-run Mac QR is a focusa-connect-v1 JSON handoff offer; generic phone camera shows raw JSON. Intended flow requires operator to open a VPS/public Focusa Connect Page and scan the Mac QR there, but current VPS room resolved to local-only http://127.0.0.1:8787/connect/... and public hostname probe 404s. Mac callback listener is ready at LAN http://192.168.1.59:<port>/..., causing expected macOS incoming-network prompt. The architecture must be fully portable to any VPS or local machine: discover/require reachable server_url, support local LAN/Tailscale/tunnel/public URL, expose manual completion payload fallback, and make UX explain why phone camera raw JSON is not success.

FirstRunConnect visibly exposes manual paste completion fallback when callback/public Connect Page is unavailable. 3. UI copy explains: generic phone camera showing JSON is expected; open Focusa Connect Page first. 4. Version mismatch between CLI and daemon is repaired or blocked with exact command. 5. Docs/tests cover VPS public URL, local-only, LAN, and Tailscale/tunnel pairing modes. Evidence citations required before close.

PORTABLE ARCHITECTURE SPEC LANDED: docs now require host-neutral transport-verified pairing across localhost same-machine, LAN/private IP, Tailscale/Funnel, Cloudflare/ngrok, reverse proxy, direct VPS public URL, or future hosted Focusa. title: MCP tool layer should match focusa doctor --json surface (single-round-trip 'what is broken')
description:
## Problem

The Focusa MCP tool layer (`focusa_project_identity`, `focusa_tool_doctor`, `focusa_trajectory_view`, etc.) returns **structured records with implicit status**, not error messages with reasons. When an agent or operator asks "what's broken?" or "why is this card `degraded`?", the tool responses are projections that drop the actionable detail the underlying daemon produces.

In contrast, `focusa doctor --json` (the underlying CLI) already returns the full structured report: `status`, `summary`, `next_action`, `why`, `commands`, `recovery`, `details.checks[16]` (with `name`/`status`/`path` per check), `readiness_categories`, `warnings`, `evidence_refs`, and `docs`. The MCP tool layer is a partial projection of this surface, and the projection hides the bits an agent needs to act.

## Reproduction

Run from any project under the Focusa MCP (this is what an agent did in a recent session on `/home/focusadev/perpetua`):

```
$ focusa project_identity
{
  "project": "perpetua",
  "status": "degraded",
  "confidence": "medium",
  "stack": "unknown",
  "workspace": "rust-monorepo",
  "urls": { "local_only": true, "root": "http://localhost:8080" },
  ...
  "degraded": true
}
```

There is **no `degraded_reasons` field.** The reason `status=degraded` is implicit: `stack=unknown` (no manifest), `urls.local_only=true` (no live server), `workspace=rust-monorepo` was operator-supplied, not tool-verified. An agent reading this response cannot tell what to fix first.

Compare with the underlying `focusa doctor --json`:

```
$ focusa doctor --json | jq '.status, .summary, .next_action, .why'
"blocked"
"1 doctor check(s) blocked; readiness categories split runtime/source/release planes"
"Run the recovery command for the first blocked check, then re-run focusa doctor"
"Spec92 requires one agent-first command center covering health, contracts, workpoint/work-loop, telemetry, cache, Pi skills, Mac app, release proof, Guardian, and cleanup readiness."
```

The CLI version returns:
- `status: "blocked"` (specific)
- `summary` (one-sentence explanation)
- `next_action` (the exact command)
- `why` (the Spec92 reason)
- `recovery` (commands to run)
- `details.checks[16]` with `name`/`status`/`path` per check
- `readiness_categories` (split by runtime/source/release plane)
- `warnings`, `evidence_refs`, `docs`

The MCP version returns **none of these.** The agent has to make 4-5 tool calls + a manual synthesis to answer the question the CLI already answers in one.

## Evidence

A recent bootstrap-status workflow on the `perpetua` project (continuous_id `focusa-cont-focusa-53795608-...`) required:

1. `focusa_project_identity` → `status=degraded, confidence=medium`
2. `focusa_project_verify` → `verified=false, status=mismatch, confidence=low`
3. `focusa_tool_doctor` → `workpoint=not_found, work_loop=blocked, recommended=REQUIRED NEXT: run focusa_trajectory_view...`
4. `focusa_trajectory_view` → `current=missing, gap=Trajectory gap unclear until desired end state and current verified state are both present`
5. `focusa_resource_mode` → `mode=normal, within_budget` (the *only* clean card)
6. Manual synthesis by the agent to produce a 1-line answer to the operator's question

The answer could have been: `focusa doctor --json | jq '.status, .details.checks[] | select(.status == "blocked") | .recovery'`. One call.

## Proposed fix

Make the MCP tool layer match the daemon's `focusa doctor --json` surface. Specifically:

### P0 — One-call doctor (matches existing CLI)

Add a `focusa_doctor --detail` MCP tool that returns the same shape as `focusa doctor --json`. Acceptance:

```bash
focusa_doctor --detail
```

Returns a flat array of cards:

```json
{
  "readiness": "blocked",
  "cards": [
    {
      "card": "project_identity",
      "status": "degraded",
      "reason_codes": ["NO_MANIFEST", "NO_LIVE_URL", "OPERATOR_SUPPLIED_HINT"],
      "fix": "Phase 0.5 writes go.mod and svelte/package.json; systemctl starts the server."
    },
    {
      "card": "workpoint",
      "status": "blocked",
      "reason_codes": ["WORKPOINT_NOT_FOUND"],
      "fix": "focusa_workpoint_checkpoint --project-root <root> --mission <m> --next <n>"
    }
  ],
  "recommended_next": "focusa_trajectory_observe --auto"
}
```

### P0 — Explicit `degraded_reasons` per card

Each MCP tool that returns `degraded` (or any non-`ok` status) must include a `degraded_reasons: [...]` array. Each reason is a typed code with a `fix` string. The agent reads the codes, looks up the fix, applies it, re-runs the tool.

### P1 — `focusa_trajectory_observe --auto`

The trajectory card returns `current=missing` because no `observed_state` has been asserted. The tool should accept a verb that derives `observed_state` from the project (last commit, doc count, manifest presence, server health) without requiring the agent to write a sentence. Acceptance: `focusa_trajectory_observe --auto` fills `observed_state` automatically and re-runs `trajectory_assess`.

### P1 — `focusa_project_verify` returns the relationship

`status=mismatch` is currently a black box. The tool should return `saved_scope`, `current_scope`, and `relationship` (`informational` / `blocking` / `supersession`) so the agent knows what to do.

### P2 — Workpoint `next` re-validates against live state

Workpoints with `partial handoff` re-validate their `next` field against the live state. If the action has been completed, surface: `"next action satisfied; suggest re-targeting"`.

## Why this matters

The Focusa doc inventory already establishes the principle: **"agent's first move on any app error is to read the logs"** (Spec 102 / Spec 92 / Spec 105). The tool layer that delivers logs to the agent must be a single round-trip, not a multi-call synthesis.

Currently, asking "what's broken?" via the MCP tool layer is a 5-call exercise. Asking the same question via `focusa doctor --json` is a 1-call exercise. The MCP layer is a partial projection that drops the actionable detail. The fix is to make the projection match the source.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `focusa_doctor --detail` (or equivalent) returns a flat array of cards with `card`, `status`, `reason_codes`, and `fix` per card.
2. Every MCP tool that returns a non-`ok` status includes an explicit `degraded_reasons` (or equivalent) array.
3. `focusa_trajectory_observe --auto` works without requiring the agent to write a sentence.
4. `focusa project_identity --json` includes the same `degraded_reasons` array as `focusa doctor --json` surfaces.
5. The "what's broken?" question is answerable in 1 round-trip via the MCP tool layer, matching the existing `focusa doctor --json` capability.
